1993756.steps:
Ian added two LAN to WAN UPE policies as follows:
  1. Allow everything to bentley.eng.sonicwall.com using an FQDN address object, with no ULA requirement.
  2. The default policy to allow everything else, with users allowed set to Trusted Users
  I have all SSO mechanisms disabled apart from RADIUS Accounting SSO.
  The issue here is that when I try to browse to http://bentley.eng.sonicwall.com I see different behavior depending on whether or not RADIUS Accounting SSO is enabled.
  RADIUS Accounting SSO enabled: the connection fails reporting that the site can’t be reached.
  RADIUS Accounting SSO disabled: the connection gets redirected to the login page.
  Both of these are wrong - the connection should be allowed straight out (there is no ULA requirement in the Bentley rule). The fact that it is getting redirected is due to what is reported in GEN7-23452, so ignoring that here, the question is why does enabling/disabling RADIUS Accounting SSO affect the redirection?
  Things like RADIUS Accounting SSO, Endpoint Security SSO and 3rd Party SSO API are passive in that they send notifications of logins/logouts, and the firewall can do nothing to send requests to them or to wait for anything from them. So having the policy code try to trigger/wait for SSO when only RADIUS Accounting is enabled, as it’s apparently doing here, does not make sense.
  The only SSO mechanisms that are applicable for the policy code to decide that it needs to request/wait for SSO are:
  SSO agent authentication is enabled.
  TSA is enabled and the connection is coming from a user at a terminal server.
  NTLM is enabled and the connection is HTTP.
1993756.title: GEN7-23395 - UPE: Enabling RADIUS Accounting SSO affects redirection to login
